title: Terraform Drift Detection

description: Infrastructure drift from declared IaC state means manual changes broke the single source of truth. Causes unpredictable behavior and deployment failures.
value: Detecting terraform drift detection early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Run `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` on schedule in CI/CD. Forward plan output to Splunk via HEC. Exit code 2 = changes detected (drift). Alert on any drift in production workspaces.
visualization: Table (workspace, resource, drift), Single value (drifted resources), Bar chart.
knownFalsePositives: A plan can show a diff right after a release while state catches up, or when we intentionally tuned something in the console during an emergency. We confirm the workspace and the window before we treat it as unplanned drift.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=devops`.
• Install and configure Custom input (Terraform CLI output, CI/CD integration) with the modular input for `terraform:plan`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Run `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` on schedule in CI/CD. Forward plan output to Splunk via HEC. Exit code 2 = changes detected (drift). Alert on any drift in production workspaces.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=devops sourcetype="terraform:plan" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=devops sourcetype="terraform:plan"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.1_terraform_drift_detectio_1"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `terraform:plan` in `index=devops` to detect terraform drift detection. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_1_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (workspace, resource, drift), Single value (drifted resources), Bar chart..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Custom input (Terraform CLI output, CI/CD integration) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of terraform drift detection so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
